video_title: Pt. 2 Grading Citrini's Viral Crypto Portfolio
gist: Part two of 0xResearch grading the tokenization-themed crypto portfolio (auto-captions garble the author's name): the panel would sharply overweight Uniswap (10-15%+ vs 4%) as the trading layer where tokenized-asset value accrues, treat Aerodrome as a short-term Base/catalyst trade dragged by ~2x emissions-to-revenue, see LayerZero and Chainlink as narrative plays lacking token-market fit, back Backpack as a ~$4B pre-IPO equity proxy, like Syrup as a cheap but distribution-constrained lender, and hold Pendle and Ondo at small 3% weights.

insights.claim: Bitcoin is holding up relatively well against equities despite last week's large VIX spike; on the weekly timeframe it remains in an uptrend and is just looking for a weekly higher low, though a return to August-September style vertical moves may take more time.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Treat the pullback as noise inside a weekly uptrend; watch for a confirmed weekly higher low before expecting acceleration.

insights.claim: Bitcoin and major crypto assets held up through an equity and AI-trade sell-off and BlackRock ETF fears, which Sam attributes to improving crypto fundamentals rather than pure price beta.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Relative strength vs equities during risk-off is a sign crypto fundamentals are starting to matter; watch for decoupling.

insights.claim: A Coinbase research letter argued that while the S&P 500 is only ~2% off its highs, most of its constituents are actually in a bear market and the index is held up by AI names; combined with peak fear, this makes the setup constructive for accumulating crypto ahead of the next leg up.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Narrow index breadth plus peak fear is framed as a buy-the-dip setup for crypto rather than a top signal.

insights.claim: Flows are rotating into an 'anti-AI trade', moving into bonds and other assets away from AI equities.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Rotation out of AI leadership could weigh on the index while benefiting duration and alternative assets.

themes.theme: Aerodrome: Base proxy vs emissions drag

insights.claim: The popular Aerodrome bull case is a catch-up trade: Uniswap trades at roughly 50x while Aerodrome trades at roughly 7-9x, with an upcoming V3 launch expanding Aerodrome to Ethereum, Robinhood chain and other EVM chains as a catalyst.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Multiple-gap and multichain launch are the stated catalysts; size it as a trade into the upgrade.

insights.claim: Post fee-switch, Uniswap on Base has remained highly competitive with Aerodrome, holding TVL and volume share, and existing Robinhood-chain launchpads are built on Uniswap, so Aerodrome's expansion to other EVM chains is unlikely to take much share quickly.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Discount expectations of rapid Aerodrome share gains on new chains; incumbency and launchpad integrations favor Uniswap.

insights.claim: Aerodrome's emissions-to-revenue ratio is hovering around 2x, meaning that if emissions are counted as spending it spends about double its revenue, so its apparent multiple discount to Uniswap is smaller once weekly ve-token emissions are netted off.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Adjust DEX multiples for emissions; Aerodrome can be viewed as running unprofitably on that basis.
insights.quote: if you count emissions as spending, you know, then they're spending double what they're they're taking in in revenue

insights.claim: Uniswap's token spending works as an annual growth-fund budget of UNI rather than ongoing ve-style emissions, so even accounting for it Uniswap appears much more profitable than Aerodrome.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Compare DEX profitability net of incentives, not on headline fees.

insights.claim: Since Coinbase launched tokenized equities on Base, Aerodrome has become the number-two DEX for tokenized equity volume, with its share rising almost week on week as the main DEX provider for those assets.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Aerodrome is a direct beneficiary of Coinbase's tokenized-equity distribution; track its weekly share.

insights.claim: Kunal views Aerodrome as a short-term trade into its upgrade catalyst and the tokenization theme rather than a long-term hold, and disagrees with a 7% portfolio weight, arguing Uniswap deserves a much higher weighting.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Rotate Aerodrome into a tactical position and overweight Uniswap within a tokenization basket.

insights.claim: Aerodrome is probably the best liquid way to get exposure to Coinbase's Base distribution since Base has no token, though Sam fundamentally prefers Solana's market structure and DEX activity over the Coinbase/Robinhood ecosystems.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Use Aerodrome as the Base proxy trade, but recognize the panel's structural preference for Solana venues.

insights.claim: Catalysts for Aerodrome's upgrade skew to the upside with little room for disappointment, but Luke would still weight Uniswap above Aerodrome because of Aerodrome's emissions-to-revenue profile.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Asymmetric event trade into the upgrade; key watch item is how much Ethereum mainnet market share Aerodrome captures.

insights.claim: Aerodrome's upcoming catalysts include multichain expansion plus a unification with Velodrome and a change to its token model.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Token-model changes can reprice the asset; watch the merger terms and new emissions schedule.

insights.claim: Aerodrome once handled about 90% of on-chain FX volume (non-USD pairs like EUR/USD) but is now only barely the leader, roughly even with Uniswap, with FX activity spreading across L2s and EVM chains including Robinhood chain and Ethereum.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Aerodrome's FX moat is eroding; on-chain FX is becoming a contested Uniswap-led multichain market.

themes.theme: Uniswap as the tokenization trading layer

insights.claim: Uniswap offers a barbell exposure: on the institutional side, V4 hooks enable permissioned pools (launched in July) handling KYC and transfer requirements for tokenized assets, and a Japanese bank is building a custom trading interface on hooks; on the retail side, hooks power novel launches and Robinhood-chain meme coin trading.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Uniswap captures both institutional tokenization and speculative retail flows, making it a core holding for an RWA thesis.

insights.claim: Uniswap is the number-one DEX for tokenized equity volume, with much of that activity coming from Robinhood chain.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Leadership in tokenized-equity DEX volume positions Uniswap as the main value-accrual point if tokenization scales.

insights.claim: If another 'Robinhood season' of on-chain activity arrives, possibly helped by hints of a large grant into Robinhood chain, Uniswap is the best DEX to play that trade.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Watch for a Robinhood chain grant program as a catalyst for Uniswap volumes.

insights.claim: Uniswap's roughly 50x multiple is high versus DEX peers that typically trade at 7-16x, but the panel argues it is justified because tokenized-equity volumes are up about 100x year to date and the addressable tokenized-asset market is large.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Pay up for growth: the panel accepts a premium multiple given the growth runway in tokenized assets.
insights.quote: But something like tokenized equities volumes um they're up 100x year-to-date. And like that's something I'd pay a high multiple for.

insights.claim: Uniswap is running at roughly $100 million in annualized UNI burn after a long period when investors left it for dead with no clear value accrual.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: The fee switch turned UNI into a cash-flow asset; burn scale supports the re-rating.

insights.claim: Uniswap's market share of tokenized-equity spot DEX volume peaked at about 64% during the Robinhood mania and is now about 24%, still the leading position.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Share has fallen materially from peak; monitor whether Uniswap holds pole position as competitors launch.

insights.claim: September was Uniswap's best month, driven largely by Robinhood-chain meme coins, and the host expects a similar share in October.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Strong recent revenue momentum supports near-term fundamentals.

insights.claim: Uniswap has been the third-largest protocol by token buybacks, behind Pump and Hyperliquid, for seven consecutive months and is likely heading for an eighth, a fact the host thinks is under-discussed.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Under-appreciated buyback scale is a potential re-rating driver for UNI.
insights.quote: Uniswap has been third on the leaderboard for 7 months in a row

insights.claim: The whole panel would raise Uniswap from its 4% weight to at least 10-15% in a tokenization-themed portfolio, reasoning that value from tokenized assets will accrue primarily to the trading layer where Uniswap leads.
insights.speaker: Kunal, Sam, Luke, host
insights.so_what: Consensus overweight: Uniswap should be among the top allocations in an RWA basket.

insights.claim: Uniswap Labs' long track record, multiple distribution layers and partnerships such as with Japan's SMBC make it the DeFi venue TradFi is most familiar and comfortable with, which matters when institutional CEOs choose partners.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Brand and track record are a moat for winning institutional tokenization deals.

insights.claim: The interop market is moving toward infrastructure that lets canonical asset issuers run burn-and-mint cross-chain workflows rather than intent- or pool-based models, because canonical burn-and-mint is infinitely scalable; LayerZero holds the vast majority of this market and won Tether for its OFT standard.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Favor interop providers that own the canonical issuer standard; Tether's choice is a strong signal for LayerZero.

insights.claim: RWA issuers may start on one chain but will likely issue on as many chains as possible in the long run, needing an out-of-the-box cross-chain workflow, which is a tailwind making ZRO the best instrument for growing institutional issuance on-chain.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: ZRO is the cleanest exposure to multichain institutional issuance.

insights.claim: ZRO's unlock and supply schedule remains an overhang: buybacks of roughly $50-100 million a year (figure unverified by the speaker) may not offset potentially hundreds of millions in emissions and unlocks.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Supply overhang dampens the bull case; track net buyback vs unlock flow.

insights.claim: LayerZero's buybacks so far equal only about 0.25% of total supply against large monthly unlocks, so the token is a narrative play on tokenization and partnerships rather than a fundamental one, with its Atlas chain as a possible infra-premium catalyst.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Trade ZRO on partnership and tokenization-narrative momentum, not cash flows.

insights.claim: Sam would allocate little or nothing to interop tokens, preferring heavier weights in DEXs and L1s because interop token value accrual is a black box to him.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Interop tokens may lag if investors favor more legible value-accrual sectors.

insights.claim: The panel's consensus is that LayerZero has product-market fit and narrative-market fit but not token-market fit.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: A useful lens for any infra token: strong product does not guarantee token accrual.
insights.quote: So, I think it's agreement that Layer Zero has product market fit, narrative market fit, but just maybe not token market fit at the moment.

insights.claim: Chainlink offers a similar cross-chain workflow to asset issuers but LayerZero holds about 90% of settled volume; Chainlink runs buybacks via its reserve yet discloses nothing about its top line or whether revenue is recurring or one-off integration deals, so Luke ranks LINK below ZRO on investability.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Chainlink needs better financial disclosure to be investable; it is a narrative position, not a fundamental one.
insights.quote: Uh so I think Chainlink in particular is a project that needs substantially more uh transparency and disclosure on its fundamentals and financials for it to become investable.

insights.claim: Over the very long term, much of interop is solving problems that would disappear if financial activity consolidates onto a single chain with globally shared state, and Luke expects market share to become far more top-heavy than today.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Long-term bear case for interop tokens and bull case for whichever L1 wins consolidation.
insights.quote: a lot of interop is solving for problems that don't need to exist

insights.claim: NEAR-based chain abstraction is processing significant volume across multiple L1s by holding wallets natively on each chain, bypassing the need for a LayerZero OFT or Chainlink CCIP integration.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Alternative interop architectures could compete with issuer-standard models.

insights.claim: Backpack issues equities on Solana that can move between the traditional financial system and Solana within seconds, giving them the most legitimate claim to tokenized equity and letting Solana prop market makers quote with confidence, producing the best spreads measured on-chain, competitive even with TradFi pricing.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Redeemability drives tighter spreads and market quality; a structural edge for Solana tokenized equities.

insights.claim: Roughly 20% of Backpack's token supply can convert into equity about a year after an IPO (subject to staking for around four years and jurisdiction rules), so the token should trade roughly in line with the market's expectation of Backpack's future IPO value.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Treat the Backpack token as a pre-IPO equity proxy; value it off expected IPO valuation.

insights.claim: Backpack's implied valuation is around $4 billion if tokens represent 20% of equity, which Sam frames as the risk-reward if it can reach competitive scale with Robinhood or Coinbase; he would weight it at least 10% versus its 5% weight.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Benchmark Backpack's implied value against Coinbase/Robinhood to size upside.

insights.claim: Backpack under CEO Armani has spent years building regulatory infrastructure and key hires across jurisdictions to become a regulated house of finance (perps, cards, banking), the opposite approach to Hyperliquid, and employee equity lockups align with token unlocks.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Regulatory-first positioning could pay off as tokenized equities and neobank features scale.

insights.claim: Backpack token holders are approaching half a million, most holding under $100, a distribution similar to typical brokerages.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Broad retail distribution supports its neobank ambitions.

insights.claim: Kunal would rather bet on Robinhood or Coinbase to win the integrated exchange plus tokenized-equity race, and would put higher weight on trading layers (Uniswap on EVM, Raydium on Solana) or money markets (Kamino, Morpho) where tokenized assets are actually used and value is generated.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Value accrual from tokenization likely sits with trading and lending venues rather than issuers or newer exchanges.

insights.claim: Syrup showed notable relative strength in deposits and outstanding loans through the 2026 bear, and its syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT products are widely used as yield-bearing collateral for borrowing and looping on money markets; a Bitcoin bull plus rising rates would let it monetize a larger loan book at higher rates, while it remains one of the cheaper lending names.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Cheap, levered play on a recovery in on-chain yields and BTC-backed borrowing demand.

insights.claim: Syrup's key gap is fintech distribution: Robinhood's savings vault is powered by Morpho, with the bulk of deposits allocated to Ethena and about 20% to Syrup, and Syrup has won Kraken but needs more such integrations to bring in high-velocity TVL.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: New fintech/exchange distribution deals are the catalyst to watch for Syrup.

insights.claim: Syrup recently turned on buybacks, which have been increasing month on month, and trades at a cheap multiple.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Growing buybacks at a low multiple support the fundamental case.

insights.claim: Lending protocols are less reflexive to the upside than DEXs and L1s in an RWA thesis, so Sam would cap the total lending allocation around 5-10%.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Size lending as a diversifier, not the high-beta core of an RWA basket.

insights.claim: As AI makes software easier to build, software itself becomes less of a moat, and distribution, partnerships and licenses become the durable moats for early crypto players.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Favor protocols with locked-in fintech distribution and licenses over pure tech differentiation.

themes.theme: Pendle: cyclical V2 vs Boros upside

insights.claim: Pendle is the marketplace for high-yield zero-coupon bonds; yield-bearing asset issuers overspend on incentives to list there, money markets profit from PT collateral with very high loan-to-deposit ratios, and Pendle has historically held 90%+ liquidity share versus rivals like Spectra and Exponent.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Pendle is the dominant go-to-market venue for new yield assets; its cycle tracks new-issuer launches.

insights.claim: Pendle V2 activity is concentrated around new yield-bearing asset launches with incentive programs and is not durable as maturities roll off, with the Ethena flywheel as the case study.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Expect V2 revenue to be episodic; don't extrapolate incentive-driven spikes.

insights.claim: Pendle's annualized revenue has fallen from about $80 million at the 2025 peak to about $10 million amid one of the worst crypto yield bear markets, the third-longest stretch where on-chain yields traded at a discount to short-term Treasuries.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Pendle is a levered bet on a recovery in on-chain yields versus Treasuries.

insights.claim: Pendle's long-term upside lies in Boros, its venue for hedging perpetual-futures funding and cost of carry across crypto and RWA perps, which Luke thinks could become a nine-figure revenue line, though traction does not yet support that within one to two years.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Boros adoption metrics are the key long-term catalyst; revenue there should be stickier and less cyclical.

insights.claim: Institutional off-chain asset issuers driving the RWA tailwind are unlikely to run points programs like crypto-native issuers, so Pendle V2 will not monetize the RWA narrative well; Luke considers Pendle's 3% weight fair.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Don't buy Pendle as an RWA proxy; buy it as a yield-cycle and perps-hedging bet.
insights.quote: I don't really think that these institutional off-chain asset issuers that is the whole tailwind for the RWA complex are are going to be running points programs the way the crypto native priors have

insights.claim: Ondo is one of the largest tokenized-equity issuers with partners like BlackRock and has begun monetizing via perps and spot products, but its roughly $2B market cap and $4B+ FDV with large unlocks make the valuation unappealing, so a 3% weight is fair.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Strong product metrics but valuation and unlocks cap upside; keep it a small position.

insights.claim: Backpack has issued about 10 times fewer tokenized equities than Ondo but did more spot volume in those assets last month, and Sam views trading volume as the best indicator of real demand.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Weight tokenization plays by trading volume, not issued supply; Ondo's supply lead hasn't translated into usage.
